subject: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency Options for FinBank
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finbank.eu>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency Options for FinBank

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for a clear discovery call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope options properly.

Summary of needs you shared:
- Production data must remain in the EU for EU customers (no cross-border storage).
- APAC user base (~15% of traffic) needs lower-latency access from Tokyo/Singapore and would prefer regional residency if possible.
- Strong preference for isolated environments for banking workloads; open to Dedicated capacity in EU if Private VPC/on-prem is not strictly required for first phase.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2, data processing addendum with explicit EU data residency, and audit log retention 12 months.

Clarifying questions:
1) For APAC traffic, is cross-border processing strictly prohibited, or acceptable if data at rest stays in the EU but transient compute happens in APAC?
2) Do you have a procurement timeline/deadline we should align to? (I know you mentioned end of Q3)
3) Any strict latency SLOs for APAC (p50/p95) we should design around?

Next steps we propose:
- Share our quick scoping matrix (attached) comparing Hosted (regional pinning), Dedicated EU pools, and Private VPC/on-prem tradeoffs.
- Technical SRE deep-dive to validate latency/egress and confirm whether Dedicated meets your isolation requirements. (30–45 min)
- Procurement path: we can assemble a DATA RESIDENCY addendum and SOC2 evidence package once scope is agreed.

I've attached a scoping matrix to capture the tradeoffs; will follow up with times for an engineering call.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0126

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency Options for FinBank

Hi Karthik —

Thanks — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- EU residency requirement applies to all production customer data (including embeddings and logs) — no long-term cross-border storage. Short-lived caches for inference are acceptable if clearly documented and encrypted, but we prefer compute and storage both in-region where possible.
- For APAC: for Phase 1 the APAC user subset can tolerate EU-at-rest with APAC compute only if latency < 200ms p95. If latency is higher we need a regional deployment in APAC (might be Dedicated or Private depending on procurement).
- Procurement: target signing window is mid-September; procurement has asked for a clear pricing delta between Dedicated and Private + an estimate of time-to-onboard.

For the SRE call, please include someone who can speak to cross-region routing and egress accounting. I've looped procurement on this thread.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Infrastructure Risk | FinBank EU
elena.rossi@finbank.eu

(On a side note, Tom from our APAC team is copied — he'll confirm latency targets for Tokyo/Singapore.)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-23T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: Deployment & Data Residency Options for FinBank

Elena — thanks for the clear constraints; good context. A few notes on capability and next steps:

Quick capability summary (high level):
- Hosted API (regional pinning): We run regional clusters and can pin processing to an EU region to keep data in-region for processing and storage. Hosted is fastest to onboard but does NOT provide tenant-level VPC isolation or guaranteed single-customer hardware.
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPU pools in EU only; provides tenancy isolation and predictable throughput. Meets most banking isolation requirements and reduces noisy-neighbor risk.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full customer-controlled VPC or on-prem package with private control plane. This is the strictest compliance posture and supports air-gapped/on-prem installs.

Notes on cross-region routing & egress:
- We can configure ingress routing so EU traffic stays in EU clusters. Cross-region fallbacks are opt-in and documented; by default we will not route EU production to APAC.
- Egress charges and data transfer for cross-region compute are measurable per-route and we can provide an estimate based on expected traffic mix.

Suggested next steps:
1) SRE deep-dive (we'll bring our infra eng who runs region routing) — proposed slots: Tue 2026-05-26 09:00-10:00 UTC or Wed 2026-05-27 15:00-16:00 UTC.
2) We'll prepare a Dedicated vs Private one-pager with expected on-board time and indicative pricing delta.
3) Start a mutual action plan doc (shared Drive) capturing procurement milestones.

Attachment: region-capabilities.pdf (detailed capability list and network diagrams).

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
